import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_state = inputs["target_state"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    
    # Ensure proper types
    target_state["order_id"] = target_state["order_id"].astype("int64")
    target_state["last_seq"] = target_state["last_seq"].astype("int64")
    cdc_events["seq"] = cdc_events["seq"].astype("int64")
    cdc_events["order_id"] = cdc_events["order_id"].astype("int64")
    
    # Remove duplicates by seq (at-least-once delivery)
    cdc_events = cdc_events.drop_duplicates(subset=["seq"])
    
    # Sort by seq to process in order
    cdc_events = cdc_events.sort_values("seq").reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Initialize new_state from target_state
    new_state = target_state.copy()
    
    # Track when each order becomes deleted (first D that removes it)
    deletion_seq = {}  # order_id -> seq of the delete that made it absent
    
    # Track all orders ever touched
    touched_orders = set(target_state["order_id"].values)
    touched_orders.update(cdc_events["order_id"].values)
    
    # Process events by order_id
    for order_id in cdc_events["order_id"].unique():
        order_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["order_id"] == order_id].sort_values("seq")
        
        # Check if order exists in target_state
        order_in_state = order_id in new_state["order_id"].values
        
        if order_in_state:
            last_seq = new_state.loc[new_state["order_id"] == order_id, "last_seq"].values[0]
        else:
            last_seq = -1  # No row means no replay guard
        
        # Apply each event in seq order
        for _, event in order_events.iterrows():
            seq = event["seq"]
            op = event["op"]
            
            # Replay guard: skip if seq <= last_seq for existing orders
            if order_in_state and seq <= last_seq:
                continue
            
            if op in ["I", "U"]:
                # Insert or update
                if order_in_state:
                    # Update existing row
                    idx = new_state[new_state["order_id"] == order_id].index[0]
                    new_state.loc[idx, "status"] = event["status"]
                    # For U with NULL amount, keep existing amount; otherwise use event amount
                    if op == "U" and pd.isna(event["amount"]):
                        pass  # Keep existing amount
                    else:
                        new_state.loc[idx, "amount"] = event["amount"]
                    new_state.loc[idx, "last_seq"] = seq
                else:
                    # Create new row
                    new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                        "order_id": [order_id],
                        "status": [event["status"]],
                        "amount": [event["amount"]],
                        "last_seq": [seq]
                    })
                    new_state = pd.concat([new_state, new_row], ignore_index=True)
                    order_in_state = True
                # Clear deletion record when re-created
                if order_id in deletion_seq:
                    del deletion_seq[order_id]
                last_seq = seq
            
            elif op == "D":
                # Delete
                if order_in_state:
                    new_state = new_state[new_state["order_id"] != order_id].reset_index(drop=True)
                    order_in_state = False
                    # Record the first delete that removes this order
                    if order_id not in deletion_seq:
                        deletion_seq[order_id] = seq
                last_seq = seq
    
    # Build tombstones: orders that are in deletion_seq (had a delete as final state)
    tombstone_rows = []
    for order_id, deleted_seq in deletion_seq.items():
        tombstone_rows.append({
            "order_id": order_id,
            "deleted_seq": deleted_seq
        })
    
    if tombstone_rows:
        tombstones = pd.DataFrame(tombstone_rows)
    else:
        tombstones = pd.DataFrame({"order_id": pd.Series(dtype="int64"), "deleted_seq": pd.Series(dtype="int64")})
    
    # Ensure proper dtypes for output
    new_state = new_state.astype({
        "order_id": "int64",
        "status": "object",
        "amount": "float64",
        "last_seq": "int64"
    })
    
    tombstones = tombstones.astype({
        "order_id": "int64",
        "deleted_seq": "int64"
    })
    
    return {
        "new_state": new_state,
        "tombstones": tombstones
    }
